note: The frontend builds and links against ../PS5_Vulkan 8b311e3 with the red/blue compensations withdrawn, and every gate replays. The withdrawal is visible in the build's own patch report: 0014's format substitution, 0075's core-frame RGBA upload and 0077's menu colour and cached-frame ownership are exchanged for the upstream text they replaced, so the frontend uploads libretro's little-endian XRGB8888 into a VK_FORMAT_B8G8R8A8_UNORM image the driver samples in that same byte order. The driver archives were frozen before the build and re-hashed unchanged after it, and the build identity - which covers those archives and is compiled into the title - was recomputed from tools/build-title.sh's own input list and matched.

gfx/drivers/vulkan.c: withdrawn (patches/series, 0077: preserve original core pixels across cached frames)
gfx/drivers/vulkan.c: withdrawn (patches/series, 0077: upload decoded menu images as RGBA)

human_check: Owner, after launching the published build on the console: "this version of RetroArch is flawless. Colors are accurate now even with red/blue compensation gone." That is the acceptance of the withdrawn path: the menu, the core frames and the transition between them draw with the correct channels while the frontend keeps libretro's own byte order. It is an owner observation and not a distilled capture - no klog run was started for this launch and no trace or kernel log was collected, so the record is the owner's words plus the deployment read-back in deploy.json. PPSSPP was not exercised by this run.
